result:
I made one change, in `meterbill/invoices/builder.py`. `build_invoice` now looks up the tax rate once per country for each invoice and reuses it for the other lines. The tenant and issue date are the same for every line of an invoice, so the rate can only vary by country.

The existing tests pass (376). I haven't timed it, and I didn't have the October dataset, so I can't confirm the run is now fast. I'd expect a large drop, because `TaxResolver.rate_for` re-reads and re-parses both JSON files on every call, and the builder called it once per line. Each invoice now makes one lookup per distinct country instead of one per line.

I kept the change inside `build_invoice` and left the resolver alone. Its documented behaviour is that data files are read on every lookup, so edits between lookups are picked up. A cache inside the resolver would end that. An invalid or missing rate also still raises `TaxError` at the same point as before.

If you time the run and it's still slow, the next step is caching the parsed tax files in the resolver across invoices. That would change the read-on-every-lookup behaviour, so I'd want your go-ahead first.
